title: Residual-dimension obstructions for null-projected supersymmetric Yang-Mills theories — submission package
description:
Residual-dimension obstructions for null-projected supersymmetric Yang-Mills theories. Version 2.2.0 holds the fourth version of the Hexagon preprint in the folder hexagon-v4 (NullProjectedSYM_v4.pdf, 41 pages, its TeX ZIP with the Python programs in anc/, unpacked source, arXiv tarball, Hexagon portal fields and AI provenance file), replacing https://hexagonmath.org/2610.00471v3. The Main Theorem is now a classification: a null-projected super Yang-Mills theory with a Majorana-Weyl gaugino and k null vectors exists in signature (s,t) if and only if s+t-2k = 10 and s-t in {8, 0, -8}, or s+t-2k = 2 and s = t (Corollary 5.15). Sufficiency comes from Theorem 5.12 (Nishino's theories carried by a complex isometry to every signature with residual dimension ten, among them 9+9 and 9+17) and Theorem 5.14 (theories with residual dimension two in every (k+1)+(k+1), with vanishing cubic terms and off-shell closure). Theorem 7.3 shows that no contraction of the source rescues the signatures (11+8n)+3 and their companions with n >= 1, including 27+3, and Proposition 7.5 that several gauginos with their own parameters do not either. Theorem 7.6 shows that gauginos mixed by their transformation rules force s = t and residual dimension 2, 4 or 6, and Lemma 7.8 with Proposition 7.9 that the remaining condition holds for residual dimension 4 and 6. Theorem 7.11 shows that a bilinear gauge bracket that is not a Lie bracket changes nothing, except to force residual dimension two when it is not antisymmetric, and Proposition 7.14 that nonlinear transformation rules of the forms B1 to B4 leave the classification unchanged. Appendices E and F check these results with contraction_check.py (32 checks) and residual_two_check.py (50 checks), and Appendix G checks Section 7.4 with mixed_check.py (122 checks). Citations of unrefereed preprints were replaced by published versions or removed.

Auxiliary fields whose equations contain gaugino bilinears, nonlinear terms outside the forms B1 to B4, and complete theories with mixed gauginos in residual dimension 4 or 6 with k >= 1 lie outside these results; Remark 7.16 explains why no statement about the superalgebra alone can exclude every theory.

Verification scope: No general Lean formalisation is claimed. The proofs are written in the manuscript; the gamma-matrix calculations are supplementary finite numerical checks.

Earlier preprint versions: https://hexagonmath.org/2610.00471v1, https://hexagonmath.org/2610.00471v2 and https://hexagonmath.org/2610.00471v3. Version 2.1.1, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23789066, removed the note that followed the abstract; its mathematics is that of version 2.1.0, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23788708. Version 2.0.0, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23787988, holds an earlier package of the fourth version.
